content.content:
## Concept

### Pitch

The bottom panel of the [RightSidebarScope](../index.md#right-sidebar-scope), beneath the referenced files and the understanding: the subagents and background commands the harness started for the running task, each shown in the colour of the mode that started it, with how long it has been running, so one that seems stuck can be seen and stopped.

### Shape

#### Description

It lists the background tasks the harness started for the run, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../../../scope/harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) keeps them: its subagents, the agents it started, and its background commands, the shell commands it ran in the background, such as a long build. A background task of any other kind isn't shown.
It is shown only once the run has started one, and takes no room before. One row per background task, in the order they started, subagents and commands together, each 24 pixels tall, 8 pixels in from the panel's edges: a spinner while it is at work, then a tick, a cross, or a dash for how it ended, done, failed, or stopped, beside a small icon for its kind, a robot for a subagent and a terminal for a command, in the theme's muted grey, then what it was started to do, in small text, cut off with an ellipsis, muted once it has ended. For a subagent that is its description, and for a command the command itself, on one line, in monospace. Its tooltip gives what it was started to do, and beneath, muted, its kind, "Subagent" or "Command", and what it is doing or how it ended. The panel is only as tall as its rows need, up to 30% of the sidebar's height, scrolling beyond that.

#### Elapsed

At the right of each row, 8 pixels in from the panel's edge, is how long it has been running, from when the harness said it started, in extra small muted tabular figures, as a task's elapsed time is written beside its status: "0:42", "12:05", "1:02:33". While it is at work it counts up every second; once it has ended it stops at how long it ran. What it was started to do is cut off before the time rather than running beneath it.

#### Stopping

A row at work can be stopped, from a Stop button: a small ghost button with a stop icon, 18 pixels square, which takes the place of its running time while the row is hovered, whose tooltip reads "Stop this subagent" or "Stop this command". Clicking it stops only that background task, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../../../scope/harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says: the task the run is for and every other background task carry on, and nothing else in the panel or the task's output changes. Once clicked, the button is disabled and the row's spinner stays until the harness notifies its end, when it shows a dash for stopped, as any stopped one does. A row that has ended has no Stop button, and neither does one whose run can't stop it on its own, as one whose input is already closed, where the task's own Cancel button stops everything still going.

#### By Mode

Each background task is shown according to the mode of the task that started it, as the [PromptModesScope](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours modes: its row has a bar 2 pixels wide down its left edge in that mode's colour, and its spinner and tick are drawn in it too, while a cross or dash keeps its own colour. A background task's mode is the mode its task was sent in, and for a step of a chain, the step's own: the spec step and a spec follow-up are Spec's, and the code step is Code's, never Chain's purple. Its tooltip names the mode, "Started by the Code task", "Started by the Spec step", and so on. A task whose mode isn't known, as one from the history saved before modes were, has no bar and keeps its spinner and tick in their own colours, its tooltip reading "Started by the task". A Chain task on its own, before its code step has been sent, is the chain's spec step, so its background tasks are Spec's and labelled "Spec".
While a chain runs, the panel keeps the background tasks of each of its steps, not only the step running: they are grouped by step, in the order the steps ran, each group headed by a small label in its mode's colour, "Spec", "Code", or "Spec follow-up", with the step running last. A task that isn't part of a chain has one group, and no label. Once the run is over, the sidebar slides back with them all, as it says.

        its own; the task's Cancel button stops it with the run.

        It is shown only once the run has something to show in it, and takes

        command, in the theme's muted grey, then what it was started to do, in
        small text, cut off with an ellipsis, muted once it has ended. For a
        subagent that is its description, and for a command the command
        itself, on one line, in monospace. Its tooltip gives what it was
        started to do, and beneath, muted, its kind, "Subagent" or "Command",
        and what it is doing or how it ended. The panel is only as tall as its
        rows need, up to 30% of the sidebar's height, scrolling beyond that.

    elapsed:
        At the right of each row, 8 pixels in from the panel's edge, is how
        long it has been running, from when the harness said it started, in
        extra small muted tabular figures, as a task's elapsed time is written
        beside its status: "0:42", "12:05", "1:02:33". While it is at work it
        counts up every second; once it has ended it stops at how long it ran.
        What it was started to do is cut off before the time rather than
        running beneath it.

    stopping:
        A row at work can be stopped, from a Stop button: a small ghost button
        with a stop icon, 18 pixels square, which takes the place of its
        running time while the row is hovered, whose tooltip reads "Stop this
        subagent" or "Stop this command". Clicking it stops only that
        background task, as the @{HarnessIntegrationScope} says: the task the
        run is for and every other background task carry on, and nothing else
        in the panel or the task's output changes. Once clicked, the button
        is disabled and the row's spinner stays until the harness notifies its
        end, when it shows a dash for stopped, as any stopped one does. A row
        that has ended has no Stop button, and neither does one whose run
        can't stop it on its own, as one whose input is already closed, where
        the task's own Cancel button stops everything still going.

    byMode:
        Each background task is shown according to the mode of the task that
        started it, as the @{PromptModesScope} colours modes: its row has a
        bar 2 pixels wide down its left edge in that mode's colour, and its
        spinner and tick are drawn in it too, while a cross or dash keeps its
        own colour. A background task's mode is the mode its task was sent
        in, and for a step of a chain, the step's own: the spec step and a
        spec follow-up are Spec's, and the code step is Code's, never Chain's
        purple. Its tooltip names the mode, "Started by the Code task",
        "Started by the Spec step", and so on. A task whose mode isn't known,
        as one from the history saved before modes were, has no bar and keeps
        its spinner and tick in their own colours, its tooltip reading
        "Started by the task". A Chain task on its own, before its code step
        has been sent, is the chain's spec step, so its background tasks are
        Spec's and labelled "Spec".

        While a chain runs, the panel keeps the background tasks of each of
        its steps, not only the step running: they are grouped by step, in
        the order the steps ran, each group headed by a small label in its
        mode's colour, "Spec", "Code", or "Spec follow-up", with the step
        running last. A task that isn't part of a chain has one group, and no
        label. Once the run is over, the sidebar slides back with them all,
        as it says.

content.text:
I changed the spec so the SubagentsPanel shows only work going on apart from the main thread, plus ordinary commands once they've run long. `piton check` reports no problems, `piton build` wrote 79 files, and the new text appears in the refreshed reference.

**"Long-running" means 15 seconds.** That was my choice; it's one number in the spec if you want it shorter or longer.

## What changed in the spec

All edits are in `spec/ui/components/right-sidebar/subagents/index.pi`, the `description` section (`.claude/reference/ui/components/right-sidebar/subagents/index.md#description`).

- **Purpose:** the panel is for what goes on apart from the main thread, so you still see it while the main thread waits, pauses or has finished its turn.
- **Subagents:** every subagent is shown, whether the main thread waits on it or it runs in the background.
- **Commands:**
  - Background commands are always shown.
  - An ordinary command (a Bash call the main thread waits on) appears only once it has run 15 seconds without its result coming back. Its time counts from when it started, and it sits among the other rows by start time.
  - A command that finishes within 15 seconds never appears, not even briefly.
- **Never shown:** commands a subagent runs, and every other tool call. All of them stay in the task's output table as before; the panel just leaves them out.
- **Long waited-on commands:**
  - They don't hold the run open.
  - They end when their result comes back, done or failed, or when the run ends.
  - Their tooltip kind reads "Command, waited on".
  - They have no Stop button, since only background tasks can be stopped on their own. The task's Cancel button still stops them.
- **Subagents the main thread waits on:**
  - They end when the harness reports their end, or when their tool call's result comes back, whichever is first.
  - They can be stopped only where the harness gave them a task id. Otherwise they have no Stop button.
- **Showing the panel:** it appears once the run has something to show in it, not before.

The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1791131709-FilterSubagentsPanelForBackground.understanding.md`.

## Anchors the code should follow
- `SubagentsPanel`: `#description` for the filtering and the 15-second rule. `#elapsed`, `#stopping` and `#by-mode` are unchanged but apply to the new rows.
- `HarnessIntegrationScope`: `#feeding`, for how background tasks are tracked and stopped by id.
- `TaskTableScope`: `#types`. All tool calls, short commands included, stay in the task's output table.

The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors still need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings before they can be used. None of them were needed here.
